title: Wild Parameters And Endo-Classes
body_html:
Wild Parameters And Endo-Classes

Let $W_F$ be the Weil group of $F$, and let

$$ WD_F=W_F\times\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb C) $$

be the Weil-Deligne group. Let $P_F$ be the wild inertia group.

Write

$$ W_F\backslash\widehat{P_F} $$

for the set of $W_F$-orbits of irreducible continuous representations of $P_F$. If $[\rho]$ is such an orbit, let $\ell([\rho])$ be its orbit length and define

$$ \dim([\rho])=\ell([\rho])\dim(\rho). $$

A wild $\operatorname{GL}$-parameter over $F$ is a finitely supported section of

$$ (W_F\backslash\widehat{P_F})\times\mathbb N \longrightarrow W_F\backslash\widehat{P_F}. $$

Equivalently, it is a finitely supported function

$$ f:W_F\backslash\widehat{P_F}\to\mathbb N. $$

Its degree is

$$ \deg(f)= \sum_{[\rho]} \dim([\rho])f([\rho]). $$

The draft denotes the set of wild parameters by $\mathscr{WP}(F)$ and the degree $N$ subset by $\mathscr{WP}_N(F)$.

The current TeX states that there is a canonical bijection

$$ \mathscr E(F)\to W_F\backslash\widehat{P_F} $$

compatible with local Langlands and cuspidal support, and that this induces a commuting diagram between irreducible $\operatorname{GL}_N(F)$ representations, Langlands parameters, endo-parameters, and wild parameters.

Draft Caution

The compatibility is cited in the TeX. This node records the draft's intended input; it does not prove the cited local Langlands compatibility.
